new_entities.name: Warfarin after a change in leafy-green intake
aliases: warfarin after vitamin K diet change
warfarin with altered green vegetable intake
new_entities.description: Warfarin treatment during periods of changed or inconsistent dietary vitamin K intake, especially from leafy green vegetables.

new_entities.name: INR variability
new_entities.description: Fluctuation in international normalized ratio control during vitamin K antagonist therapy.

edges.effect_quant: In a dietary-record cohort, each additional 100 micrograms/day of vitamin K averaged over 4 days lowered INR by about 0.2, and a controlled trial found that adding only 25 micrograms/day of vitamin K from a multivitamin reduced INR by a median 0.51 in vitamin-K-depleted warfarin users.
edges.population: adults receiving warfarin or other vitamin K antagonist therapy in outpatient anticoagulation management
edges.mechanism: Warfarin inhibits the vitamin K cycle, so sudden increases or erratic swings in dietary vitamin K intake can counteract anticoagulation and shift INR control away from the therapeutic range.
edges.summary: The practical hazard is not leafy greens themselves but changing intake patterns while on warfarin. Evidence consistently suggests that low, erratic, or suddenly increased vitamin K exposure can destabilize INR, whereas a stable dietary pattern produces more predictable anticoagulation.
edges.caveats: This edge does not support blanket avoidance of green vegetables; it supports consistency. Individual sensitivity varies with baseline vitamin K status, genotype, target INR range, and overall anticoagulation management quality.

evidence.citation: Khan T et al 2004 Br J Haematol
evidence.notes: Dietary vitamin K influences intra-individual variability in anticoagulant response to warfarin.

effect_quant.comparator: INR change associated with higher average dietary vitamin K intake over 4 days

evidence.citation: Sconce E et al 2005 Thromb Haemost
evidence.notes: Patients with unstable control have a poorer dietary intake of vitamin K compared to patients with stable control of anticoagulation.

effect_quant.comparator: lower mean daily vitamin K intake in unstable versus stable anticoagulation control

evidence.citation: Kurnik D et al 2004 Thromb Haemost
evidence.notes: Over-the-counter vitamin K1-containing multivitamin supplements disrupt warfarin anticoagulation in vitamin K1-depleted patients. A prospective, controlled trial.

effect_quant.comparator: median INR change after adding 25 micrograms/day vitamin K1 in vitamin-K-depleted patients
